title: Chronometric slice quarantine with shadow-circuit and smoke replay
author: Ava Chen
description:
Context: We need safer, lower-latency detection and automated isolation when new model variants cause subtle regressions only visible if you consider traffic slices over time (e.g. time-of-day or chronological cohorts). Existing canary/quarantine mechanisms are good for static slices but do not express time-bound behavior or shadow-based gated isolation. This PR introduces a 'chronometric slice quarantine' primitive and a lightweight 'shadow-circuit' bridge for replaying a compact smoke of production traffic to validate hypotheses before widen/rollback.

What this PR does: implements a quarantine controller that treats slices as first-class, time-aware units. Key ideas: (1) chronometric policy windows: a slice can be quarantined for a sliding time horizon (N minutes/hours) and automatically released after telemetric criteria stabilize; (2) shadow-circuit: when suspicious signals are triggered we spin up an isolated shadow bridge that replays a selected smoke set (prefix sampling + session affordances) against the candidate model off the main path; (3) smoke replay harness: deterministic compact replay (configurable sample seeds) to reproduce errors and exercise KV-cache warm paths; (4) rollback advisor hooks: quarantine events feed the rollback advisor with provenance and small synthetic deltas to recommend immediate rollback or staged drain.

Why: improves detection and response for regressions which manifest as temporal bursts or session-coherent failures, reduces noisy full-cutrollbacks by enabling targeted quarantine and deterministic reproductions to aid SREs and on-call.

Design summary and components changed: single continuous description below. Controller and policy: rollout/controller/chronometric_quarantine.go — new controller implementing time-windowed slice locks and backoff semantics; quarantine policy objects allow window length, sample budget, and fuzz factors for early-release. Shadow bridge: integrations/shadow/circuit.go — lightweight bridge that captures a sampled prefix and forks it into a shadow lane with session stickiness and KV-warm replay. Smoke harness: telemetry/smoke/replay.go and tests under tests/integration/rollouts_smoke.yaml — deterministic replay with seed-based sampling and reproducible KV-cache priming. Rollback advisor integration: rollout/rollback_advisor.go — small adapter to transform quarantine evidence into priority suggestions. Runbook: docs/runbooks/rollouts.md updated with operational playbook and CLI commands.

Testing and verification: unit tests added for controller state transitions (stable -> quarantined -> released), e2e smoke replay test that runs shadow-circuit against a toy variant, integration manifest for canary scenarios, and a small load test verifying that shadow-circuit imposes <2% extra latency on the main path in sampled scenarios. CI: all checks green after two reruns of flaky integration tests.

Checklist: - [x] Controller implementation and unit tests - [x] Shadow bridge + replay harness - [x] Integration test manifest - [x] Runbook and CLI docs - [x] Telemetry dashboards (minimal metrics added) - [x] Rollback advisor hooks

Backward compatibility: quarantine policies are additive; existing rollout flows unchanged unless a policy is attached. No migration needed for existing customers.

How to exercise locally: make an env var ROLLUP_QUARANTINE=true and run ./devctl rollout simulate --manifest tests/integration/rollouts_smoke.yaml; to reproduce smoke replay use TELEMETRY_REPLAY_SEED=42 and inspect telemetry/trace/span ids for the shadow-circuit lane.

Notes: This PR contains behavior-sensitive surface area (quarantine auto-release). We intentionally default to conservative windows in the config and require explicit opt-in in release profiles for autoscale-heavy workloads.

Related work: complements ENG-2197 (session-anchored canaries) and ENG-2412 (shadow fidelity metrics); sup ticket SUP-4422 contains customer logs that motivated the design.

review_conversation: Diego Morales: Can you clarify why we need a separate shadow-circuit vs existing shadow lanes? The isolation and deterministic seeding is the main rationale — reduced blast radius for reproductions.

Ava Chen: Reply: shadow-circuit is intentionally narrow: it binds session prefixes and a compact KV priming step so replay is deterministic and safe to run repeatedly without affecting caches used by the live lanes.
Priya Suresh: Please add an opt-out flag for high-throughput customers; we risk added load if sampling not controlled.
Ava Chen: Added QUARANTINE_SAMPLE_CAP and conservative defaults; updated docs and integration manifest to make caps explicit.
Liam O'Neill: unit tests look good, integration was flaky but passed on rerun. Approving after CI stabilization.
Diego Morales: Approved and left minor nits on logging verbosity which are addressed in the last commit.
release_notes: Adds a chronometric slice quarantine controller and a deterministic shadow-circuit replay harness to improve temporal-slice regression detection and targeted rollback recommendations. Opt-in via policy; conservative defaults ensure no added load by default.
high_level_summary: New time-aware quarantine and shadow replay primitives that make rollouts safer for temporal/cohort regressions; integrates with rollback advisor for automated recommendations.
operational_impact: Low by default (opt-in). Operators can configure window sizes and sample caps. Added runbook and CLI flags for simulation and manual quarantine management.
